title: Gallery holds ~1.5 GB of VRAM until you navigate away
description: Scrolling a 161-asset gallery takes Vision from 410 MB to 1858 MB of dedicated VRAM and never releases it - measured, flat for 13 minutes. Every video card promoted by the grid IntersectionObserver gets a permanent <video preload=auto>; the observer unobserves after promoting, so a card can never be demoted. Add a releaseMedia/resumeMedia primitive on MpiGalleryGrid and call it when the gallery stops being visible and when a generation is dispatched, so the UI is not holding VRAM the model needs.
acceptance: MpiGalleryGrid suspends and restores hover-video promotion internally - _releaseMedia(reason) tears down every promoted <video> via the existing _removeHoverVideo path, _resumeMedia(reason) re-promotes what is on screen once the LAST hold drops. Deliberately NOT exposed on instance.el: both callers live inside the grid, so a public method would be unused API

Promotion stays SUSPENDED while released - a _mediaSuspended flag checked inside _promoteVideo - because IntersectionObserver.observe() fires immediately for already-intersecting targets and would re-promote the visible band on the next tick, freeing nothing
Release fires when the gallery stops being visible (a Flow opens over it), and resume fires when it is visible again
Release fires when a generation is dispatched, and resume fires when the queue drains - so the GPU is free for the model at the moment it is needed
While suspended, an explicit hover on a single card may still promote it (one decoder, not 161) so the gallery stays usable during a long generation
The generating card's live preview path (updatePreview / resetPreviewClip, preview-bus) is NOT affected by suspension

A card scrolled further than DEMOTE_MARGIN_PX out of view demotes itself, via a SECOND IntersectionObserver at a wider margin than the promote one - the gap is hysteresis, since a single shared boundary thrashes a card parked on the edge. Scrolling back re-promotes it

Measured: the same tour (open a big project, scroll the gallery end to end, open a flow) no longer leaves Vision resting near 1858 MB, and Vision's dedicated VRAM at generation dispatch is materially lower than it is today
docs/gallery.md documents the release/suspend contract, and js/components/types.js documents the new grid methods
